cells.tense: Here you are with the pen, and the pattern you cut is holding.
cells.act: go once toward the thing that draws you and see what it is up close
cells.ask: Go once this week toward the want you keep turning over before acting on it — before you've decided whether it's right. Look at it up close. That's the whole move, and nothing has to follow it.
cells.core:
You see the shape of a thing before the talk has finished, and here that reading feeds the momentum instead of narrating it. When it's going well, a thought lands and the body already knows what it's for — not certainty, exactly, but the way opening while you're still walking it. The pattern and the aim arrive together, and the aim moves.
Nothing is blocked at this level, and nothing needs digging out. The pull is just easy to spend on more thinking instead of one move. You'll know it if you've been holding a decision steady in your head for a week without doing anything with it. Close that gap once this week — the direction wants acting on, not explaining.
cells.sheetLine: You see the shape and the aim at the same time.
cells.verb: cutting patterns into shape with the mind
cells.place: at the point where the road begins to narrow

cells.tense: The pattern keeps being finished in advance, before the moment you're actually in.
cells.act: let the structure act instead of announcing it
cells.ask: Make the next move you'd normally lay out for someone first, and make it bare. No plan explained, no reasoning set in front of it, no framing after. Just the move and what it does.
cells.core:
There's a version of this where you've solved the whole road ahead before you're standing on it — every fork pre-decided, every objection pre-answered. The analysis is sharp enough to do that, and it feels like being prepared. But the goal gets handled instead of reached, and conclusions get handed to the people in it before they've been met where they are.
Nothing is wrong with the reading itself. It's that the reading has moved in front of the living, and everything downstream is calibrated to a future that hasn't happened. So drop one move without the preamble. The structure is still there, doing its work. You'll notice it doesn't need the announcement.

cells.tense: You stopped at a door that's already behind you and haven't turned around.
cells.act: walk toward what connects, leaving what does not
cells.ask: Take one real step toward the person or thing that actually draws you, from where you've been standing still. Not the step you'll take after some other Tuesday. Just the one, and see if the ground under it is solid.
cells.core:
The pattern is still in you — the cutting, the reach — but it isn't moving anything. Analysis comes and doesn't land on a road; it goes to somebody else's project or nowhere at all. That's not laziness, and it's not confusion. The engine is idling where the last decisive moment left it.
Under that, something did get put down, and the read here is that whatever ended, ended. The person on the other side already knows what the person who doesn't leave their chair won't say. So one real step toward whatever pulls at you — not toward the plan, toward the thing itself. You don't need to know how far. Go once and look.

cells.tense: You're the one cutting the pattern, and the credit has been left on the table.
cells.act: follow the pull of what might be felt, a little way
cells.ask: Follow one pull a little way this week — the thing that keeps asking for you and keeps getting filed under nothing. An hour of attention, no outcome owed. See where it actually goes.
cells.core:
The reading and the aiming are running your life right now — the calls you've made, the way things moved because you saw them move — and if someone asked what did it, you'd probably say the situation, or the moment, or just that's how it was. Your hand is in more of this than you've filed as yours. Not a character flaw. An unaddressed account.
The draw is the thing to follow, not the reasoning about it. Something has been pulling at you — a direction, a person, an open question — and you've been analyzing it from a distance instead of walking to it. Go once. See it close up. Whatever it turns out to be, you were the one who went.
